transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Um... I guess I'm here because of my sleep. I barely sleep in any useful way anymore. I just... lie awake, replaying client models. Then I wake up at 3 or 4 in the morning with my stomach tight. I just go to work feeling like I never actually rested.
How long have you been experiencing this sleep problem?
Um... a while. I guess about three years now. It started right around the time the merger reorganized our Caribbean-market division at work. So... yeah, since then.
Do you often feel anxious or on edge during the day, outside of the times when you're lying awake at night?
Um... no, not really. I don't think so. I'm mostly just... drained during the day.
Do you have nightmares?
Um... no. Not really. I don't... I don't think I even dream much anymore. It's mostly just... lying there in the dark.
Do you find yourself repeatedly thinking about the same things or feeling like you need to repeat certain actions over and over?
Um... no. I don't think so. I don't really do anything like that.
Has the sleep problem changed in severity or frequency when you're not working, such as during weekends or vacations?
Um... no. I don't think so. It's... it's pretty much the same. Weekends don't really make a difference.
Do you think the stress from your job is contributing to your sleep problems?
Um... I don't really know. Work is... it's just work. I'm not sure if it has anything to do with my sleep. It's hard to tell.
Did the sleep problems start immediately after the merger at work or was there a delay?
Um... I don't think there was a delay. It's... it's been going on for about three years now. Pretty much ever since the merger reorganized our Caribbean-market division.
Do you think the merger and subsequent changes at work have had any effect on your overall stress levels?
Um... I guess? I haven't really... thought about it like that. It's just work. You just kind of... do what you have to do every day. I don't really know if I'd call it stress.
Do you feel more relaxed and able to sleep better when you are on vacation or completely removed from work-related tasks?
Um... I don't really know. I haven't... I don't take a lot of vacations. So I couldn't really tell you. Even when I do have a few days off, I just... I haven't really noticed a difference.
Do you think your sleep gets worse on days when you have a lot of work or stressful work tasks?
Um... no, not really. I don't think there's a pattern like that. It's just... pretty much the same every night, regardless of what's on my desk.
Is there something specific about your job or work environment that you think might be contributing to your sleep problems?
I don't think so. It's... it's just a normal office environment. I just do my work and that's it. There isn't really anything specific that stands out to me.
Is there a particular aspect of your work that you find most challenging or worrying?
No, not really. It's... just work. I just do what I need to do. I don't really worry about it.
Is there something about the merger or the reorganization of your division that still bothers you or affects your daily work?
I mean... I guess. It's just... it's been about three years now. Ever since they merged and reorganized our Caribbean-market division. It's just been like this since then.
Is there something specific about the time of the merger and the reorganization of your Caribbean-market division that you think might have triggered your sleep problems?
I don't know. It's... it was just a lot of changes all at once. I don't really know if there was one specific thing. It just all happened, and... here we are.
Is there something specific about your work or the merger that you think about when you're lying awake at night?

I mean... mostly just the numbers. I'll just lie awake replaying client models in my head. I... I barely sleep in any useful way anymore. And then I usually end up waking up at 3 or 4 in the morning anyway. My stomach gets all tight, and... I just go to work feeling like I never actually rested.
Is replaying client models in your head at night related to any specific stress or anxiety you feel about your work?

I don't... I wouldn't really say it's a specific stress. It's just work. The numbers are just... there. I don't really know why it happens. It's just what my brain focuses on when it's quiet, I guess.
Is there something specific about your work with client models that worries you or causes you stress?

I suppose... I mean, I guess it's just that I'm having a harder time with them lately. Spreadsheets used to be second nature to me. Now... it takes me hours. I just sort of lose the thread of what I'm doing. I end up rereading the same assumptions over and over. And even then, I still worry I've missed something obvious before I have to present it. It's just... frustrating.
Is worrying about presenting client models correctly the main thing that's on your mind when you're lying awake at night?

I don't... I'm not really sure if I'd call it the main thing. It's not always a specific worry about the presentation itself. The numbers just... they just kind of cycle through my head. It's mostly just noise, really. I don't know.
Do you think your sleep problems would improve if you were to change jobs or take a break from your current work responsibilities?
I don't know. I haven't really thought about it. I mean... I guess I've been doing this a long time. I'm not sure what else I'd do, or if it would even make a difference. It's just... I don't know.
